title: Bonsai Trees in Your Head: How the Pavlovian System Sculpts Goal-Directed Choices by Pruning Decision Trees
description: Empirical modelling paper. Forty-six participants were trained to criterion on a deterministic six-state environment (two buttons, two transitions from each state, a reward or loss on each transition) and then planned sequences of 2 to 8 moves to maximise total reward; three groups differed only in the size of the large loss (-70, -100 or -140 pence). Models compared: full look-ahead tree search, 'Discount' (a fixed probability of stopping the search), 'Pruning' (a separate, higher stopping probability after a large loss), learned Pavlovian values, a pruning-plus-learned model, loss-aversion variants and a habitual SARSA model; fitted by maximum a posteriori estimation with empirical priors (EM) and compared with integrated BIC. Subjects pruned after large losses even when it was costly, and pruning was related to subclinical mood scores.
